REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
AND SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
THURSDAY - DECEMBER 13, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

2.
Invocation
The California Court of Appeal has concluded that sectarian prayer as part of the City Council meetings is not permitted under the Constitution.
Invocation

Pledge of Allegiance

Presentations
Presentations
6.
Public Comments and Suggestions
This section is reserved for comments related to Consent Calendar Items and items not listed on the Agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council/Successor Agency. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the City Council/Successor Agency, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.
7A.
Approval of Minutes
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of November 19, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Minutes of November 19, 2018
7B.
Approval of Registers of Demands
7B.1.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated December 13, 2018 (COUNCIL).
City Register of Demands
7C.
Approval of the completion of the biennial review of the City of Cerritos, Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency, and Cerritos Public Financing Authority conflict of interest codes pursuant to the Political Reform Act of 1974 and submit proposed amendments for approval (COUNCIL/AGENCY/AUTHORITY).
Waive full reading of and adopt A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL, SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, AND CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY ADOPTING THE AMENDED CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODES, AND REPEALING RESOLUTION NOS. 2016-29, SA 2016-2, AND CPFA 2016-1 (COUNCIL/AGENCY/AUTHORITY).
Agenda Report
8.
Public Hearings
8A.
Review and consideration of a written appeal of a decision of the Cerritos Property Preservation Commission denying a request to remove a parkway tree adjacent to the property located at 17117 Ely Avenue, Cerritos, California (APN 7025-006-010), Property Preservation Commission Case No. TR 2018-10 (COUNCIL).

9.

9A.
Review and consideration of award of a contract, RFP No. 1356-18, Project No. 19201, for engineering design services for the Cerritos Swim Center (COUNCIL).

Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for Fiscal Year 2017-18 (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
Exhibit 1
10.
Legislative Items
10A.
Report on pending legislation.
10B.
Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.
Closed Session
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AND A
SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY HELD
ON DECEMBER 13, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Joey Venegas, Generations Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division Teen
  Volunteers Samuel Avalos, Aryana Desai, and Cameron Campbell.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  A Proclamation was made as follows:

  Janice and John Dawson (50th Wedding Anniversary).

  A surprise Presentation was made as follows:

  Vince Brar (Retirement/Service Commemoration)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Ashish Gupta spoke regarding assistance his family has provided in the community
  and submitted a document for the record.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding a neighborhood potluck, a Measure BB community
  group, various Cerritos media outlets, and economic impact studies. He expressed
  concern regarding public comments at open meetings.

  Vicki Flores requested a policy to grant a permit for a second car for Cerritos street
  parking, expressed an interest in placing such issue on an upcoming ballot, and
  inquired of the process.

  Charlie Godbee spoke regarding a notification on power pole work in his
  neighborhood and the coordination and scheduling of future similar projects.

  Francisco Martinez, Lisa Lemaster, and Jean Thompson, on behalf of Southern
  California Edison, provided an update on the Del Amo-Eric Recabling Project.
   City of Cerritos  December 13, 2018
  City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

  6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Brian Thornhill spoke regarding a recent ABC Unified School District Board Meeting
  and comments made at a previous City Council/Successor Agency meeting.

  7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

  7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of
  November 19, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of November 19, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

  7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated December 13,
  2018 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  12/13/2018  $1,640,294.31 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the completion of the biennial review of the City of Cerritos,
  Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency, and Cerritos Public
  Financing Authority conflict of interest codes pursuant to the Political Reform Act
  of 1974 and submit proposed amendments for approval
  (COUNCIL/AGENCY/AUTHORITY).

  Waive full reading of and adopt A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY
  COUNCIL, SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY,
  AND CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY ADOPTING THE AMENDED
  CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODES, AND REPEALING RESOLUTION NOS. 2016-29,
  SA 2016-2, AND CPFA 2016-1 (COUNCIL/AGENCY/AUTHORITY).
 City of Cerritos  December 13, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Approve the completion of the biennial review of the City of Cerritos, Successor
  Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency, and Cerritos Public Financing
  Authority Conflict of Interest Codes pursuant to the Political Reform Act of
  1974; and

  2. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution Nos. 2018-21, CSA 2018-3,
  CPFA 2018-1, A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY
  COUNCIL, SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT
  AGENCY, AND CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY ADOPTING
  THE AMENDED CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODES, AND REPEALING
  RESOLUTIONS NO. 2016-29, SA 2016-2, AND CPFA 2016-1
  (COUNCIL/AGENCY/AUTHORITY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of a written appeal of a decision of the Cerritos
  Property Preservation Commission denying a request to remove a parkway
  tree adjacent to the property located at 17117 Ely Avenue, Cerritos,
  California (APN 7025-006-010), Property Preservation Commission Case No.
  TR 2018-10 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Ben Stahovich, appellant, noted the root system of the subject tree is severely
  impacting his property and presented photographs for the record.

  Mr. Stahovich, nephew of appellant, spoke in support of the appeal requesting
  removal of the subject tree and/or repairs.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor
  closed the public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION DID NOT PASS: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by
  Pulido, to remand the subject appeal back to the Property Preservation
  Commission for a decision to be made by all five (5) Commission members,
  noting the absence of one Commission member at the time of the original, split
  decision.
 City of Cerritos  December 13, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  The motion did not pass (2 – 3) as follows:

  AYES:  Yokoyama, Pulido
  NOES:  Edwards, Hu, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to direct staff to
  repair the damaged sidewalk adjacent to the subject property (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business
9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract, RFP No. 1356-18, Project No.
  19201, for engineering design services for the Cerritos Swim Center (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Senior Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Award a contract for Engineering Design Services for Cerritos Swim Center,
  Project No. 19201, RFP No. 1356-18 to IDS Group, Inc. in an amount not to
  exceed $12,600; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract
  modifications that may be necessary to complete the specified scope of work
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5– 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos Comprehensive Annual Financial
  Report for Fiscal Year 2017-18 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Mike Matsumoto, Financial Consultant, and Ken Pun,
  representing the Pun Group LLC. A PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  (continued next page)
 City of Cerritos  December 13, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to receive and file
  the Fiscal Year 2017-18 City of Cerritos Comprehensive Annual Financial Report
  (COUNCIL).

10.  Legislative Items

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Yokoyama, Mayor Pro-
  Tem Solanki, and Mayor Pulido.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:50 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone_
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
